papers.title: Implicit Neural Representations for Variational Problems on Graphons
papers.abstract: We propose a neural exploratory framework for variational problems over graphons, i.e., symmetric measurable functions $[0,1]^2 \to [0,1]$, that arise as limits of dense graph sequences. Such problems are central to two parts of the mathematical literature: extremal graph theory, which studies graph parameter optimisation under given restrictions, often for those graphs with a large number of vertices, and the large deviation theory of dense random graphs, which characterises the structure of rare events through constrained graphon optimisation. We represent graphons by implicit neural networks and optimise graphon objectives by gradient descent. Our design combines three ingredients: a multi-scale sinusoidal residual architecture biased toward sharp, step-like graphons; an embedded solver that enforces a single empirical density constraint and is differentiated by implicit differentiation; and symmetry-aware Monte Carlo estimators. On generalised Tur\'an problems that previously required substantial human effort, our framework rediscovers known optimal graphons without human intervention. Applied to open instances, it produces candidate optima, including a previously unreported family of extremal structures. Applied to the variational problems from the large deviation theory of Erd\H{o}s--R\'enyi random graphs, the framework produces new candidate optimal graphons across both upper- and lower-tail regimes for multiple pattern graphs; for the case of the triangle graph and the upper-tail regime, these candidates improve upon the best-known reference construction of Lubetzky and Zhao. The structures found by our framework have also led to new theorems on the optimal graphons for both families of problems.

papers.title: Stable Set Reconfiguration in Dense Digraphs
papers.abstract: In a directed graph, a stable (or acyclic) set is a set which does not induce a directed cycle. Given a directed graph and two acyclic sets of the same size, the Acyclic-Set-Reconfiguration with Directed Token Sliding (ASR) problem asks whether one can, by iteratively replacing a vertex by an adjacent one, transform the first set into the second one, while maintaining acyclicity during the transformation. In this work, we present a study of the complexity of ASR and provide an FPT algorithm for semi-complete digraphs, when parametrized by the size of the sets being reconfigured, the directed pathwidth (or equivalently, the directed treewidth) of the instance, and a newly introduced parameter called the iteration of the reconfiguration sequence. To the best of our knowledge, the reconfiguration of stable sets has only been studied on undirected graphs, or (more recently) on sparse directed graphs.

papers.title: Structure and Exact Certification of Nonnegative Tensor Decompositions
papers.abstract: We study the structure and exact certification of nonnegative tensor decompositions supplied through rational factor matrices. Every failure of minimality or essential uniqueness contains an irreducible positive exchange between $p$ supplied terms and $q$ competing terms. A dimension count based on the Lovitz--Petrov splitting theorem bounds the effective order of such an exchange, the sum over the modes of the joint factor-span dimension minus one, by $p+q-2$, and this bound is attained at every supplied length $R\ge2$. After eliminating ambient-row variables by the Farkas lemma, the resulting semialgebraic systems have fewer than $2R^2$ real variables. For input bit length $L$, this gives a deterministic $G(R)L^{O(R^2)}$-time algorithm that computes the nonnegative rank and an exact minimum-length decomposition, decides minimality and essential uniqueness, and returns exact witnesses when either property fails. The exponent is independent of the tensor order and the mode dimensions. For Lebesgue moment tensors, positive quadrature determines the nonnegative rank and the uniqueness behavior, and some rational length-$R$ inputs force a common field of degree at least $\lfloor R/2\rfloor!$ for any exact minimum-length output. As an illustration, an implementation resolves all 114 instances left inconclusive by earlier positive-scattering criteria, of which 95 are minimal and essentially unique and 19 are minimal but nonunique.

papers.title: Subset selection problems in planar point sets
papers.abstract: Given a finite point set satisfying condition $\mathcal{A}$, the subset selection problem asks, how large of a subset satisfying condition $\mathcal{B}$ can be extracted? In this paper, we make progress on three instances of subset selection problems in planar point sets. Let $n,s\in\mathbb{N}$ with $n\geq s$, and let $P\subseteq\mathbb{R}^2$ be a set of $n$ points, where at most $s$ points lie on the same line. Firstly, we select a general position subset of $P$. This problem was proposed by Erd\H{o}s under the regime when $s$ is a constant. For $s$ being non-constant, we give new lower and upper bounds on the maximum size of such a subset. In particular, we show that in the worst case such a set can have size at most $O(n^{5/6+o(1)}/\sqrt{s})$ when $3\leq s\leq n^{1/3}$ and $O(n/s)$ when $n^{1/3}\leq s\leq n$. Secondly, we select a monotone general position subset of $P$, that is, a subset in general position where the points are ordered from left to right and their $y$-coordinates are either non-decreasing or non-increasing. We present bounds on the maximum size of such a subset. In particular, when $s=\Omega(\sqrt{n})$, our upper and lower bounds differ at most by a logarithmic factor. Lastly, we select a subset of $P$ with pairwise distinct slopes. This problem was initially studied by Erd\H{o}s, Graham, Ruzsa, and Taylor on the grid. We show that for $s=O(\sqrt{n})$ such a subset of size $\Omega((n/\log{s})^{1/3})$ can always be found in $P$. When $s=\Theta(\sqrt{n})$, this matches a lower bound given by Zhang on the grid. As for the upper bound, we show that in the worst case such a subset has size at most $O(\sqrt{n})$ for $2\leq s\leq n^{3/8}$ and $O((n/s)^{4/5})$ for $n^{3/8}\leq s=O(\sqrt{n})$. The proofs use a wide range of tools such as incidence geometry, probabilistic methods, the hypergraph container method, and additive combinatorics.

papers.title: The number of regular simplices in higher dimensions
papers.abstract: We study the extremal function $S^k_d(n)$, defined as the maximum number of regular $(k-1)$-simplices spanned by $n$ points in $\mathbb{R}^d$. For any fixed $d\geq2k\geq6$, we determine the asymptotic behavior of $S^k_d(n)$ up to a lower-order term. In particular, when $k=3$, we determine the exact value of $S^3_d(n)$, for all even dimensions $d\geq6$ and sufficiently large $n$. This resolves a conjecture of Erd\H{o}s in a stronger form. The proof leverages techniques from hypergraph Tur\'an theory and linear algebra.

papers.title: Links of minimum degree and exact covering numbers
papers.abstract: The covering number $C(v,k,t)$ is the least number of $k$-subsets, called blocks, of a $v$-set such that every $t$-subset lies in one of them. We reduce the question whether a covering with $L$ blocks exists to the classification of links. If every point of such a covering lies in at least $r$ blocks and $(r+1)v>kL$, some point lies in exactly $r$ blocks, and its link, the blocks through it with the point removed, is a $(v-1,k-1,t-1)$-covering with $r$ blocks. It then suffices to list these links up to isomorphism, to prove the list complete, and to show that no link in the list extends to a covering with $L$ blocks. Completeness is certified by one unsatisfiable formula that excludes the listed classes, so the program that lists the links need not be trusted. In general the last two steps are decided by propositional satisfiability (SAT) solving, with every formula written by two separately implemented encoders and every refutation checked by a formally verified proof checker. For links with four blocks and $t=3$ we give the classification by hand, under a condition on the parameters. As an application we determine twenty-five covering numbers with $t\in\{3,4,5\}$ in which the published lower bound was one less than the size of a known covering, among them $C(39,24,3)=9$.

papers.title: Acyclic 2-edge-coloured graphs: polynomial-time linkages and colouring hardness
papers.abstract: A path or cycle in a $2$-edge-coloured graph is alternating if consecutive edges have different colours. These objects are natural analogues of paths and cycles in graphs, and even more so in digraphs. A well-studied class is that of acyclic $2$-edge-coloured graphs, that is, those forbidding alternating cycles. In particular, (acyclic) $2$-edge-coloured graphs generalize directed (acyclic) graphs (DAGs), but the complexity of problems on DAGs is much better understood than that of the corresponding problems on acyclic $2$-edge-coloured graphs. We investigate the complexity of two such problems, whose directed counterparts are well-known. Our first result is an $n^{O(k)}$-time algorithm for the alternating $k$-linkage problem on acyclic $2$-edge-coloured graphs. This problem asks for $k$ vertex-disjoint alternating paths joining $k$ prescribed pairs of vertices. This generalizes the directed $k$-linkage algorithm for DAGs. For every fixed $k$, this also yields a polynomial-time algorithm for finding $k$ internally vertex-disjoint alternating $(s,t)$-paths, solving an open problem by Abouelaoualim et al. from 2008. We then consider the alternating chromatic number of $2$-edge-coloured graphs, defined as the minimum number of parts in a vertex partition such that each part induces an acyclic subgraph. This notion is analogous to the dichromatic number of digraphs, where it is known that deciding dichromatic number $2$ is NP-complete even on tournaments. Our second result is that deciding alternating chromatic number $2$ is NP-complete on complete $2$-edge-coloured graphs. Equivalently, deciding whether a graph can be partitioned into two induced threshold graphs is NP-complete.

papers.title: Identifying codes of Archimedean grids
papers.abstract: An identifying code of a graph is a dominating set $C$ such that the sets $N[v]\cap C$ are pairwise distinct. The minimum density of an identifying code has been studied extensively for several infinite grids. It is known to be $1/4$ for the triangular grid and $7/20$ for the square grid, whereas for the hexagonal grid the problem is still open, between $5/12$ and $53/126$. These three grids are the regular members of the family of the eleven Archimedean grids. In this paper, we start a systematic study of identifying codes in this family. We determine the minimum density for five of the nine Archimedean grids for which it was not known: it is $2/3$ for the truncated hexagonal grid $3.12.12$, $3/7$ for the truncated square grid $4.8.8$, and $1/3$ for the trihexagonal (kagome) grid $3.6.3.6$, the elongated triangular grid $3^3.4^2$ and the snub hexagonal grid $3^4.6$. All lower bounds are proved by the discharging method. For the three remaining non-regular Archimedean grids, we also obtain some bounds: the minimum density lies between $3/7$ and $13/30$ for the truncated trihexagonal grid $4.6.12$, between $1/3$ and $11/30$ for the rhombitrihexagonal grid $3.4.6.4$, and between $2/7$ and $9/28$ for the snub square grid $3^2.4.3.4$.

papers.title: Proximity Theorem and FPT Algorithm for Minimum Group-labeled Matroid Bases
papers.abstract: Let $M$ be a matroid, let $\ell:E(M)\to G$ be a labeling of its elements by an abelian group, and let $F\subseteq G$ be finite. A base is $F$-avoiding if the label sum of its elements is not in $F$. We prove that, for arbitrary costs, a min-cost $F$-avoiding base can be obtained from any min-cost base using at most $|F|$ exchanges. This resolves the weighted proximity conjecture by H\"orsch, Imolay, Mizutani, Oki, and Schwarcz. Our main technical tool is to replace the assumption of Schrijver--Seymour Conjecture in Liu and Xu's earlier work with Kemperman--Scherk Theorem. The proximity theorem combined with approaches in earlier work gives an FPT algorithm that finds a min-cost $F$-avoiding base parameterized by $|G|$. We additionally give an FPT algorithm parameterized by $|F|$, answering a question of H\"orsch et al.

papers.title: The Size of the Intersection of $q$-ary Hamming Balls
papers.abstract: The interest in studying the size of the intersection of multiple $q$-ary Hamming balls has grown due to the recent advances in DNA-based data storage systems. We present an exact formula for the cardinality of the intersection of $s$ Hamming balls of varying radii over a $q$-ary alphabet. It is known that the distances between the center points of the Hamming balls are not enough, in general, to determine the size of the intersection. Based on our formula, we are able to find more refined structural properties of the center points for determining the exact size of the intersection. Moreover, we also analyze the size of the intersection of Hamming balls with equal radii $t$ for sufficiently large $n$ when $t$ and $q$ are constants. When $s=3$, we give the necessary and sufficient conditions (for all $q\ge 2$, $q\neq 6$ and sufficiently large $n$) to obtain the maximum size of the intersection when the centers of the Hamming balls have a given minimum distance and demonstrate how to compute it using our general formula.

papers.title: Broadcast Domination Number is at Most Twice the Multipacking Number
papers.abstract: For a graph $ G = (V, E) $ with a vertex set $ V $ and an edge set $ E $, a function $ f : V \rightarrow \{0, 1, 2, . . . , diam(G)\} $ is called a \emph{broadcast} on $ G $. For each vertex $ u \in V $, if there exists a vertex $ v $ in $ G $ (possibly, $ u = v $) such that $ f (v) > 0 $ and $ d(u, v) \leq f (v) $, then $ f $ is called a dominating broadcast on $ G $. The cost of the dominating broadcast $f$ is the quantity $ \sum_{v\in V}f(v) $. The minimum cost of a dominating broadcast is the broadcast domination number of $G$, denoted by $ \gamma_{b}(G) $. A multipacking is a set $ M \subseteq V $ in a graph $ G = (V, E) $ such that for every vertex $ v \in V $ and for every integer $ r \geq 1 $, the ball of radius $ r $ around $ v $ contains at most $ r $ vertices of $ M $, that is, there are at most $ r $ vertices in $ M $ at a distance at most $ r $ from $ v $ in $ G $. The multipacking number of $ G $ is the maximum cardinality of a multipacking of $ G $ and is denoted by $ mp(G) $. It is known that $mp(G)\leq\gamma_b(G)$. In 2014, Hartnell and Mynhardt proved that $\gamma_b(G)\leq 3mp(G)-2$ whenever $mp(G)\geq2$. In 2019, Beaudou, Brewster, and Foucaud improved this bound to $\gamma_b(G)\leq 2 mp(G)+3$ and conjectured that $\gamma_b(G)\leq 2 mp(G)$. We solve their conjecture by proving that $\gamma_b(G)\leq 2 mp(G)$ for every graph $G$. Our proof is constructive and yields a linear-time $2$-approximation algorithm for Maximum Multipacking problem which improves the earlier approximation factor $2+o(1)$.

papers.title: A counterexample to Tokareva's conjecture on sums of two bent functions
papers.abstract: It is well known that the sum of two bent functions on $\mathbb{F}^n$ has algebraic degree at most $n/2$ for even $n\ge 4$. Tokareva conjectured that the converse holds: every Boolean function with degree at most $n/2$ can be written as a sum of two bent functions. The conjecture has been verified for even $n\leq 6$ and for several special classes of Boolean functions. We disprove this conjecture by showing that $x_1x_2(x_3x_4+x_5x_6+x_7x_8)$ is not a sum of two bent functions on $\mathbb{F}^8$. We extend this construction to obtain counterexamples in every even dimension $n\ge 8$. Using Shaporenko's reduction, we also obtain explicit counterexamples to Tokareva's derivative conjecture in every even dimension $n\ge 10$.

papers.title: A probabilistic construction of maximum $h$-scattered subspaces
papers.abstract: Let $1\le h\le n-2$ and $g=\gcd(n,h+1)$. We prove that, for every prime power $q$, a maximum $h$-scattered $\mathbb{F}_q$-subspace of $V(r,q^n)$ exists whenever $(h+1)\mid rn$ and $$r\ge\frac{h+1}{g}\bigl(h(n-h-2)+1\bigr).$$ In particular, for fixed $n$ and minimum distance $\delta\in\{2,\ldots,n-1\}$, $\mathbb{F}_{q^n}$-linear MRD codes of length $N$ exist for every $q$ and every sufficiently large $N$ such that $n$ divides $(n-\delta+1)N$, with a bound on $N$ depending only on $n$ and $\delta$. We take the $\mathbb{F}_{q^s}$-span of the columns of a random matrix $A$ over the algebra $R=\mathbb{F}_{q^n}\otimes_{\mathbb{F}_q}\mathbb{F}_{q^s}$, for a suitable $s$. Such a subspace is maximum $h$-scattered if and only if the kernel of $A$ contains no nonzero vector whose expansion with respect to an $\mathbb{F}_q$-basis of $\mathbb{F}_{q^s}$ has rank weight at most $h+1$. When $\gcd(n,s)=1$, $R$ is a field, and a first-moment argument, counting these vectors up to multiplication by $\mathbb{F}_{q^n}^*\mathbb{F}_{q^s}^*$, shows that with positive probability the kernel contains none of them if $s>h(n-h-2)$. When $d=\gcd(n,s)>1$, $R$ is a product of $d$ fields, and vectors vanishing in some factors lie in the kernel with larger probability. We control them by proving that, for an $(h+1)$-dimensional $\mathbb{F}_q$-subspace $D$ of $\mathbb{F}_{q^n}$, the elements of $D\otimes_{\mathbb{F}_q}\mathbb{F}_{q^s}$ vanishing outside $k$ given factors, $0<k<d$, form an $\mathbb{F}_{q^s}$-space of dimension at most $(h+1)k/d$, with equality only if $D$ is linear over a subfield of $\mathbb{F}_{q^n}$ larger than $\mathbb{F}_q$. Taking $s=gr/(h+1)$ gives the bound on $r$. Finally, if $(n-h-1)\mid(h+1)$, then for every $r$ satisfying the above inequality there is an $h$-scattered $\mathbb{F}_q$-subspace of $V(r,q^n)$ of dimension $\lfloor rn/(h+1)\rfloor$, without a divisibility condition on $rn$.

papers.title: Power Sum Varieties over Finite Fields
papers.abstract: We study a family of affine algebraic varieties over a finite field $\mathbb{F}_q$ defined by systems of power sum polynomials. Our main goal is to investigate their geometric and arithmetic properties, with particular emphasis on the structure and dimension of their singular loci. Using tools from the theory of symmetric polynomials and generalized Vandermonde determinants, we establish explicit conditions under which these varieties are complete intersections and prove that, in a broad range of parameters, their singular loci have codimension at least two. As a consequence, we derive normality and irreducibility results for both the affine varieties and their projective closures. Building on this geometric analysis, we obtain estimates for the number of $\mathbb{F}_q$-rational points and deduce effective existence results for solutions of systems of symmetric power sum equations over finite fields. Finally, we apply these results to the study of Waring's problem and to the analysis of the cost of computing a $\mathbb{F}_q$-rational point of such systems.

papers.title: Rank identifications in join-meet ideals of thin distributive lattices
papers.abstract: Let $L$ be a thin distributive lattice of rank $m+1$, and let $I_L$ be its join-meet ideal in the polynomial ring $S_L$. For $A\subseteq\{1,\dots,m\}$, let $J_A$ be the ideal obtained from $I_L$ by identifying, for every $i\in A$, the variables of the two elements of $L$ of rank $i$. We prove that $J_A$ is prime if and only if $A$ contains no turning rank and does not contain both ranks adjacent to a turning rank. In this case, $S_L/J_A$ is the toric ring obtained from Hibi's parametrization of the Hibi ring of $L$ by identifying suitable pairs of variables, and for an arbitrary $A$ we describe the saturation of $J_A$ as a lattice ideal.

papers.title: Kazhdan--Lusztig Polynomials for permutations with $P_{\mathrm{id},w}(1)=3$ and Irreducible Singular Locus
papers.abstract: We determine the Kazhdan--Lusztig polynomial $P_{\mathrm{id},w}(q)$ for permutations $w$ such that $P_{\mathrm{id},w}(1)=3$ and the Schubert variety $X_w$ has irreducible singular locus. Let $h=h(w)$ be the minimum height $w(a)-w(d)$ of a $3412$-occurrence in $w$ at positions $a<b<c<d$, with $h=1$ when no such occurrence exists. We show that $P_{\mathrm{id},w}(q)=1+q^h+q^{h+1}$ if exactly one of the patterns $3412$ and $4231$ occurs, and $P_{\mathrm{id},w}(q)=1+q+q^h$ if both patterns occur. In the latter case, $h>1$. This proves the irreducible singular locus case of a 2009 conjecture of Billey and Weed.

papers.title: Palindromic switching rook polynomials and domino-stable collections of cells
papers.abstract: Let $\mathcal{P}$ be a finite collection of cells. Two non-attacking rook configurations on $\mathcal{P}$ are switching-equivalent if one can be obtained from the other by a sequence of switches inside rectangles contained in $\mathcal{P}$. The switching rook polynomial of $\mathcal{P}$ enumerates the resulting equivalence classes according to the number of rooks. We characterize the collections of cells whose switching rook polynomial is palindromic. More precisely, we introduce a new combinatorial property, called domino-stability, and we prove that the switching rook polynomial of $\mathcal{P}$ is palindromic if and only if $\mathcal{P}$ is domino-stable.

papers.title: Principal specializations of the $t$-chromatic symmetric function
papers.abstract: We introduce the $t$-chromatic symmetric function $Z_G(\mathbf{x};t)$, a variant of Stanley's chromatic symmetric function in which the variable $t$ records the number of distinct colors used in a proper coloring. Although $Z_G(\mathbf{x};t)$ is equivalent to the chromatic symmetric function as a graph invariant, its principal specializations retain substantially more information than those of the chromatic symmetric function. This construction is motivated by the work of Bajo--Beck--Vindas-Mel\'endez on the $q$-chromatic polynomial and the conjecture of Loehr--Warrington that the $n$th principal specialization of the chromatic symmetric function distinguishes trees on at most $n$ vertices, both of which stem from Stanley's longstanding question of whether the chromatic symmetric function distinguishes trees. We determine the classes of caterpillars resulting from the second principal specialization of $Z_G(\mathbf{x};t)$, showing that the second specialization already captures some of the structure of trees. We then prove that the third principal specialization distinguishes and explicitly reconstructs caterpillars with three spine vertices as well as elongated bistars. Finally, we conjecture, based on computational data, that the fourth principal specialization distinguishes all caterpillars.

papers.title: Affine Higher Bruhat Orders
papers.abstract: The higher Bruhat orders are partial orders originally constructed by Manin and Schechtman, with an equivalent construction from Ziegler. These partial orders generalize the weak order on the symmetric group $\mathfrak{S}_n$, and the second higher Bruhat order is a poset on commutation classes of reduced words for the longest element in ${\mathfrak{S}}_n$, where covering relations correspond to braid relations. Like the weak order, each of the higher Bruhat orders is a ranked poset with unique minimal and maximal elements. Constructing analogs of the higher Bruhat orders in other settings is an area of recent interest, including recent work of Hothem for permutations in $S_{n}$. We give a construction that generalizes any interval $[\mathrm{id},w]$ in the weak order where $w$ is an element of the affine symmetric group $\widetilde{\mathfrak{S}}_n$. Our construction recovers the classical higher Bruhat orders when $w$ is the longest element in $\mathfrak{S}_n$. Paralleling the classical case, we show that the second higher Bruhat order is a ranked poset on commutation classes of reduced words for $w\in \widetilde{\mathfrak{S}}_n$, allowing us to prove a conjecture due to Elias. When $w\in \mathfrak{S}_n$, we also establish results for our higher Bruhat orders that are direct analogs of numerous results in the classical higher Bruhat orders.

papers.title: Additive energy and Fourier complexity of graphs
papers.abstract: We study the additive energy and the Fourier approximation of graph adjacency matrices labeled by a cyclic group. For a graph with $N$ vertices, $s$ edges and adjacency matrix $M$, the additive energy of its directed edge set is at most $\min\{(2s)^3,N^2\operatorname{tr}(M^4)\}$, and equality in the spectral bound holds exactly when the labeling attains the graph-energy lower bound for the Fourier ratio. Such a labeling also minimizes every best $k$-term Fourier approximation error, whose square equals the tail of the squared adjacency singular values. We prove that graphs of odd prime-power order admit an equality-attaining labeling exactly when they are cyclic Cayley graphs, and a connected example on $15$ vertices shows that equality need not imply vertex transitivity at other orders. We construct regular graph families with asymptotically maximal normalized additive edge energy and unbounded minimum Fourier ratio, one of them with density tending to one half. For dense graph sequences under uniformly random labelings, the collision dimension differs from the reciprocal squared edge density by a quantity tending to zero in probability. We also prove a quantitative stability estimate for the graph-energy bound and show why its dependence on a spectral scale cannot be omitted, even for regular graphs. For a rank-$m$ orthogonal projector we prove $m\leq D_4\leq\operatorname{FR}^2$, characterize the equality $D_4=m$ by cyclic translation invariance, and obtain a quantitative approximation by a circulant projector.

papers.title: Presheaf structures governed by oriented matroids and pseudohyperplane arrangements
papers.abstract: We study higher complements of pseudohyperplane arrangements and the specialization maps between them, induced by degenerations. We develop a presheaf formalism on oriented matroids and weak maps, which model degenerations. Our main constructions are the posets of weighted and weightwise topes, which provide functorial combinatorial models for higher complements and their specialization morphisms. Their presheaf structure yields a deletion-contraction homotopy pushout, from which we derive a uniform combinatorial proof of the integral cohomology presentation for all $n \geq 2$. This presentation is natural with respect to weak maps and identifies cohomology rings with higher Orlik-Solomon algebras extending the known formulas for linear arrangements to non-realizable oriented matroids. Finally, we equip Deligne groupoids with a presheaf structure and identify them functorially with the fundamental groupoids of the complexified complements.

papers.title: Bounded compositions and products of chains, or bi(s)nomials everywhere from de Moivre's formula to spin multiplicities and constant-sum codes
papers.abstract: How many ways are there to select $k$ objects from $n$ types when type $i$ is available in only $s_{i}$ copies? For equal bounds, this is de Moivre's problem of obtaining a prescribed total with $n$ dice, now a textbook application of the principle of inclusion-exclusion. For arbitrary bounds, the answer is encoded by the rank polynomial $\prod_{i=1}^{n}(1+x+\cdots+x^{s_{i}})$. Its coefficients enumerate bounded compositions and submultisets, give, after normalization, the probability mass function of a sum of independent discrete uniform random variables, and are the weight multiplicities of a tensor product of $\mathrm{SU}(2)$ representations. Most of these interpretations are classical but dispersed; here we place them in a common notation and document their provenance. A complement involution proves symmetry and boundary identities. For arbitrary bounds, lower-half first differences give both symmetric-chain starts and mixed-spin multiplicities, and the chain-length and irreducible-dimension profiles agree. Convolution gives log-concavity and the central mode. For equal bounds with fixed $s \geq 1$ and even $ns$, local expansions give central asymptotics with explicit $1/n$ and $1/n^{2}$ corrections for the coefficient and its first difference. A Poisson limit gives the first boundary crossover of these differences at scale $k \sim \lambda n^{s/(s+1)}$, with factor $e^{-\alpha\lambda^{s+1}}$ when the proportion of bounds equal to the fixed minimum $s \geq 1$ tends to $\alpha>0$. Central first differences include the $s$-Catalan numbers, themselves Littlewood-Richardson coefficients; central layers yield maximum-size constant-sum codebooks for hash-based signatures. Under the polynomial binomial convention, the full inclusion-exclusion transform vanishes, and the omitted terms sum to the negative of the number of bounded compositions.

papers.title: Swapping Compatible Words
papers.abstract: In 1981 Guibas and Odlyzko showed that the set $A$ of all words of a given length $n$ that avoid a given word $p$, and the set $B$ of all words of length $n$ that avoid a given word $q$, have the same cardinality iff $p$ and $q$ have the same self-border lengths. In 2024 Carrigan et. al. asked if there is a "natural" bijection between $A$ and $B$. This paper makes partial progress toward answering that question. We provide such a bijection by imposing additional conditions on $p$ and $q$, but we also obtain a stronger conclusion: there is a "natural" bijection $\Phi$ from the set of all finite words to itself such that a word $\Omega$ has a $p$ or $q$ at a given position iff $\Phi(\Omega)$ has, repectively, a $q$ or a $p$ at that same position. An algorithm is given for converting $\Omega$ into $\Phi(\Omega)$.

papers.title: Coefficient Positivity for Arborescence Ratios of Covering Digraphs
papers.abstract: For a directed graph with a chosen root, the arborescence polynomial sums the products of edge weights over all spanning trees directed toward that root. In a finite graph cover, each lifted edge inherits the variable of its base edge. At corresponding roots, the ratio of the cover's arborescence polynomial to the base polynomial is known to be an integer polynomial. We prove that every coefficient of this ratio is nonnegative, resolving the positivity conjecture of Pylyavskyy. The key to the proof is to allow fibers of unequal size and replace the permutations defining a cover by arbitrary maps. For these more general systems, we prove a stronger coefficient-positivity theorem for a determinant derived from the graph Laplacian. The enlarged class is closed under two reductions: contraction of an edge over a base loop and elimination of a base vertex. Both yield nonnegative recurrences for the relevant coefficients in terms of smaller systems, allowing an inductive proof. We also pose the problem of finding a direct combinatorial interpretation of the coefficients.

papers.title: Polychromatic blocks and explicit lower bounds for multicolour van der Waerden numbers
papers.abstract: Let $W(r,k)$ be the least $N$ such that every $r$-colouring of $\{1,\dots,N\}$ contains a monochromatic $k$-term arithmetic progression. Many of the best lower bounds for $W(r,k)$ with $r\ge3$ come from blow-up recurrences of Blankenship, Cummings and Taranchuk and of Xu, in which a known colouring is lengthened by a periodic block. Call an $h$-colouring of $Z_q$ $k$-polychromatic if every $k$-term progression with nonzero common difference meets each of the $h$ colours. The argument behind these recurrences shows that such a colouring gives $W(r,k)>q(W(r-\lceil r/h\rceil,k)-1)$ for all $r\ge h$. We show that cubic, quartic, quintic and sextic residue colourings give $k$-polychromatic blocks with $q$ much larger than $k$ (e.g. $q=1,376,317$ for $h=3$ and $k=28$), and use them to get explicit lower bounds. For three colours and $9\le k\le28$ we improve on every published bound we know of, among them $W(3,9)>4,002,705$ and $W(3,28)>159,594,201,561,100,726$. For $3\le r\le6$ and $9\le k\le28$, $77$ of the $80$ cases improve on what the published bounds give under these recurrences and the other three tie. For $r=5$ and $12\le k\le15$ the best values come from palettes that are cyclic intervals of colours indexed by quintic residues. We checked every block by exhaustive enumeration and every base colouring by computer. We also prove that the block modulus is at most $(W(2,k)-1)/(k-1)$, so the method does not improve the asymptotics. For large $k$ the largest cubic block modulus lies between $k^{4-\varepsilon}$ and $k^2 4^k$.

papers.title: Equifacetted polytopes whose facets are products of simplices: The simplicial prism case
papers.abstract: We study \emph{prismatical} polytopes, those all of whose facets are combinatorially isomorphic to the simplicial prism $\Delta^{d-2}\times\Delta^1$. In dimension three these are exactly the cubical polytopes, so the class sits naturally between simplicial and cubical polytopes. In dimension four, $\Delta^2\times\Delta^2$ is the simplest prismatical polytope and we can construct infinitely many by using connected sums. By fibreing a triangle over a triangulated polygon we construct infinitely many connected-sum-prime prismatical $4$-polytopes. Finally, we show that there are no prismatical $d$-polytopes for $d\ge5$, answering a question of Perles and Shephard.

papers.title: On the magic positivity of the Ehrhart polynomials of dilated base polytope of minimal matroid
papers.abstract: In this paper, we consider the magic positivity of the Ehrhart polynomial of dilated base polytope of minimal matroid of rank $k$ dimension $n$. We prove that for $\displaystyle 1\leq k<\lfloor\frac{n}{2}\rfloor$, the $n-k-1$ dilate of the Ehrhart polynomial is not magic positive. We also show that for sufficiently large $n$, the $n-k$ dilate of the Ehrhart polynomial is, in general, magic positive. This gives rise to a lower bound of the $m-$index of the Ehrhart polynomial.

papers.title: The number of Tverberg partitions beyond prime powers
papers.abstract: Sierksma's conjecture asserts that every affine map $a\colon\Delta_{(d+1)(r-1)}\longrightarrow\mathbb{R}^d$ has at least $((r-1)!)^d$ unordered Tverberg partitions into $r$ parts. Until now, lower bounds growing with $d$ were known only when $r$ is a prime power. As one of our main results we prove that for every integer $r\geq3$, every decomposition $r=kq+s$ into $q=p^\alpha$ a prime power, $k\geq1$ and $s\geq0$, and every affine map $a$, the number $\operatorname{Tv}(a)$ of unordered Tverberg partitions satisfies \[ \operatorname{Tv}(a)\ \geq\ \frac{q}{r!}\,\Big(\frac{q}{\alpha+1}\Big)^{\big\lceil\frac{(r-1-2s)(d+1)}{2}\big\rceil}. \]

papers.title: Saturation in three-uniform Berge hypergraphs: the five-star spectrum and the $K_4$ saturation number
papers.abstract: For a graph \(G\), a hypergraph is Berge-\(G\)-saturated if it contains no Berge copy of \(G\), but adding any missing hyperedge creates one. We determine the complete saturation spectrum of three-uniform Berge five-stars for every order. For \(n\ge7\), every integer from \(\lceil4n/3\rceil-3\) to \(2n-5\) occurs; the additional values depend only on \(n\) modulo five. The structural ingredient is a sharp bound on the remainder after deleting all complete five-vertex components: for an \(n\)-vertex, \(m\)-edge Berge-five-star-saturated hypergraph, this remainder has at most \(15(2n-m)/7\) vertices. We characterize all equality cases. We also prove that every three-uniform Berge-\(K_4\)-saturated hypergraph on \(n\ge7\) vertices has at least \(n\) edges. Together with known constructions, this determines its saturation number for every order and settles the conjecture of Chen, He, and Xie; the new lower bound covers the previously unresolved orders \(9\le n\le95\). Both arguments use the distinct representatives forced by saturation to obtain local incidence constraints. For five-stars these constraints bound the size of the remainder and characterize equality. For \(K_4\), they reduce a putative counterexample to a configuration on at most eight vertices; incidence estimates and a sharp bound on the vertices covered by short cycles in a bipartite graph exclude all remaining cases.

papers.title: The chromatic number of $\{\mathrm{ISK}_4, \textup{diamond}\}$-free graphs
papers.abstract: An $\mathrm{ISK}_4$ is a graph that is isomorphic to a subdivision of $K_4$; a \textit{diamond} is $K_4$ minus one edge; and a \textit{bowtie} consists of two triangles sharing exactly one vertex. L\'ev\^eque, Maffray, and Trotignon~(2012) conjectured that every $\mathrm{ISK}_4$-free graph is $4$-colorable. Chen, Chen, Cui, Feng, and Liu~(2021) proved this for $\{\textup{diamond},\textup{bowtie}\}$-free graphs. We prove this conjecture for diamond-free graphs. Moreover, the bound is optimal.
